# Temple Scroll Column 48 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 48 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**48:1** When you march out to war against your enemies and observe horses and chariots — an army greater in number than your own — you shall not fear them.

**48:2** For the LORD your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.

**48:3** When you draw near to battle, the priest shall come forward and address the people.

**48:4** He shall declare to them: Hear, O Israel — today you advance into battle against your enemies. Let not your hearts grow faint.

**48:5** Do not fear, do not tremble, and do not stand in dread before them.

**48:6** For the LORD your God is the one who marches with you, to wage war on your behalf against your enemies, to deliver you.

**48:7** The officers shall then address the people: Is there a man who has built a new house and not yet dedicated it? Let him depart and return to his house, lest he perish in battle and another man dedicate it.

**48:8** Is there a man who has planted a vineyard and not yet enjoyed its fruit? Let him depart and return to his house, lest he perish in battle and another man enjoy it.

**48:9** Is there a man who has betrothed a wife and not yet married her? Let him depart and return to his house, lest he perish in battle and another man marry her.

**48:10** The officers shall further address the people: Is there a man who is fearful and fainthearted? Let him depart and return to his house, lest his brothers' courage melt like his own.

**48:11** The officers shall speak to the people: Has any man built a new house and not dedicated it? Let him depart and return to his house.

**48:12** When the officers have concluded their address to the people, they shall appoint commanders over the forces at the head of the people.

**48:13** When you besiege a city for an extended period, waging war to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them, for you may eat their fruit.

**48:14** You shall not fell them — for is the tree of the field a human being, that it should endure your siege?

**48:15** Only trees that you know do not produce food — those you may destroy and fell, and you shall construct siege works against the city that wages war against you until it is subdued.

**48:16** When you encamp before a city, you shall designate an area outside the camp, and you shall go out to that area.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 48 presents the laws of warfare from Deuteronomy 20:1-20 and 23:9-14. The priestly exhortation (vv. 3-6) precedes military engagement. The officers' exemptions (vv. 7-11) reflect concern for incomplete personal obligations. The tree-preservation statute (vv. 13-15) distinguishes fruit-bearing from non-fruit-bearing trees — an early environmental ethic within military law. The rhetorical question in v. 14 is one of the Bible's most famous humanitarian arguments.*
